title: Tankers Burn in Hormuz Again. Last Time, America Went to War
description:
This week Iran's Revolutionary Guard reported three tankers on fire in the Strait of Hormuz. If it looks like a new crisis, it's the second chapter of an old one. Miss the first chapter and nothing in this week's news makes sense, so here it is in six minutes.

From 1984 to 1988, Iraq and Iran attacked hundreds of merchant ships in the Gulf. Kuwait put its tankers under the American flag, the US Navy escorted them through mined waters, the USS Stark was hit by Iraqi missiles, Operation Praying Mantis became the largest American naval battle since the Second World War, and the cruiser USS Vincennes shot down Iran Air Flight 655, killing all 290 people on board.

The Archive Paradox: today's news, and the history it is continuing.
